prompt.context: Our client is the CFO of a large multi-billion dollar consumer goods company in North America. The recent economic crisis has generated a need to drastically reduce costs in order to maintain the firm's future competitiveness. The senior executive team has decided to take cost cutting steps to achieve significant cost reduction by 2012. Since the company expects to grow its sales over the period, it has been determined that core activities such as production plans, sales, and marketing should not be affected by this initiative.
prompt.question: The CFO, who is responsible for the initiative, has approached our firm in order to: (1) develop a comprehensive understanding of cost reduction alternatives, (2) provide a recommendation on the appropriate approach and steps to execute this initiative, and (3) advise on who should be involved. The target is $500 million in cost cuts by 2012. What is your recommendation?

clarifying_info.q: What is the total cost base of the company?
clarifying_info.a: Multi-billion dollar company — exact cost base not provided; focus on identifying opportunities qualitatively.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any specific cost areas the CFO has already identified?
clarifying_info.a: No specific areas have been pre-identified; the CFO wants a comprehensive analysis.

clarifying_info.q: Is headcount reduction on the table?
clarifying_info.a: Workforce-related savings are possible as long as core production, sales, and marketing are preserved.
Yes, all alternatives are open for consideration.

framework: 1. Identify cost reduction opportunities across all non-core functional areas
2. Assess approach to implementation (how to execute the initiative)
3. Identify key players and stakeholders who should be involved

questions.prompt: What are the main cost reduction opportunities available to the client?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm broadly across people, process, technology, and supplier levers while explicitly excluding core areas (production, sales, marketing). Strong candidates will prioritize and size opportunities toward the $500M target.

questions.prompt: How should the client approach the implementation of the cost reduction initiative?
questions.guidance: Candidate should outline a structured execution roadmap: form a team, size and benchmark opportunities, restore underperforming areas, eliminate or redesign areas that are performing as designed but still have gaps, then implement with feedback loops.

questions.prompt: Who are the key stakeholders that should be involved in this initiative?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify functional experts, senior management sponsors, internal customers (functions impacted), and external stakeholders such as suppliers. Broad stakeholder coverage signals awareness of change management complexity.

brainstorming.prompt: Brainstorm all cost reduction opportunities available to the client, given that production, sales, and marketing cannot be touched.

categories.name: People & Organization
ideas: Direct productivity improvement by addressing workload imbalances

categories.name: Technology
ideas: Implement technology solutions that reduce manual work

categories.name: Location & Real Estate
ideas: Move selected back-office operations (accounting, finance) to low-cost locations
Consolidate office locations to reduce and distribute fixed costs

categories.name: Outsourcing
ideas: Outsource non-core operations such as call centers and transactional work

categories.name: Procurement & Suppliers
ideas: Implement supplier consolidation to achieve better COGS through volume leverage

recommendation: Pursue a comprehensive cost reduction program targeting the $500M goal through a combination of: (1) workforce productivity and organizational delayering, (2) technology-enabled automation of back-office functions, (3) selective offshoring/outsourcing of non-core operations, and (4) supplier consolidation for improved COGS

Prioritize initiatives by ease of implementation and magnitude of savings; quick wins (e.g., supplier consolidation, location moves) should fund longer-horizon programs (e.g., technology implementations)
risks: Future growth investments and planned capital expenditures may offset realized savings, so net cost reduction must be tracked carefully
Workforce changes carry morale and retention risk — change management and incentives are critical
Outsourcing and offshoring may introduce quality, compliance, or operational continuity risks
Without quantitative baselining of each opportunity, there is a risk of falling short of the $500M target
next_steps: Form a dedicated cross-functional cost reduction team with executive sponsorship from the CFO
Map and size each opportunity area against the cost base; benchmark versus industry peers
Run a pilot on highest-confidence initiatives before broad rollout
Establish governance and reporting cadence to track savings realization against target
